subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should isolated cron setup be allowed to use a bounded share of the job timeout budget by default, or should maintainers require an operator-configurable watchdog instead?
rationale: Current code proves the 60s ceiling remains, but changing it affects cron capacity when setup is genuinely stuck, so the final default/config policy needs maintainer intent before the issue can close.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Land the open PR or equivalent so long-running isolated setup can pass the old 60s ceiling while retaining a cap for stuck setup.

options.title: Require a config knob
options.body: Ask for an explicit operator setting and upgrade/docs proof before accepting a longer setup window.

options.title: Split by backend
options.body: Keep the generic watchdog at 60s and move only provider-specific slow startup cases to backend-owned fixes.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Land the open PR or equivalent so long-running isolated setup can pass the old 60s ceiling while retaining a cap for stuck setup.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent owner-boundary history in the cron watchdog/timer split and is the best routing candidate for the default-vs-config policy choice.
